question.text: Under Regulation 2(1)(c)(i) of the PFUTP Regulations, why is issuer misinformation that affects market price treated as fraud against investors?

answer.text: Because market prices are presumed to be manipulated
Because all market participants are presumed to be potential fraudsters
Because markets are assumed to be unable to self-correct from fraudulent activities
Because investors who trade at the affected market price are effectively misled, even though they did not rely on the false statement itself or anything derived from it other than the market price

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pages 48 and 144, Regulation 2(1)(c)(i) treats issuer misinformation that affects market price as fraud because investors are effectively misled through the market-price impact, even though they did not rely on the statement itself or anything derived from it other than the market price. The Trap: Options A, B and C state extreme positions (all prices manipulated, all participants fraudsters, markets cannot self-correct) that the regulation does not adopt. The clause is grounded specifically in the market-price transmission of misinformation. Note: The source uses the market-price transmission rationale directly; do not import doctrinal labels not present in the workbook.
